claims.statement: The signup flow calls auth.register with an auto-generated teamName ("{firstName}'s Team"), returns 202 without logging the user in, and requires email verification before authentication.

The Verify component reads email and token from query params, calls auth.verify which returns a redirect URL, then navigates the browser to that URL so the backend can redirect back with #access_token in the fragment.

The consumeFragmentToken function in App reads #access_token from the URL hash, stores it via setToken, reads ?flow=signup to set the justSignedUp signal, and clears both from browser history via replaceState.
The justSignedUp signal is a one-shot flag set only on the redirect after a fresh signup (email verification or OAuth), consumed once by the Shell for the welcome banner, and never persisted.

The Login component calls auth.login(email, password), which also loads teams in the same round trip, then navigates to '/'; on 401 it shows 'Invalid email or password'. It also surfaces a backend-handled link failure read from the ?error query param. The session token is stored in localStorage, so a hard refresh preserves the session via checkSession().
OAuth buttons navigate to {apiUrl}/auth/oauth/authorize/{provider}?noauthchallenge, where the noauthchallenge param skips the auth challenge step and the backend handles the full OAuth flow.
OAuth and email verification share the same fragment token capture mechanism: the backend redirects with #access_token in the URL hash, which consumeFragmentToken reads and stores.
Forgot password always shows the same confirmation regardless of whether the email exists (API returns 202 in both cases) to prevent email enumeration.

Reset password uses bearer-mode delivery: PATCH /auth/reset-password?delivery=body returns access_token directly in the response body, logging the user in automatically without a follow-up POST /token.

The invitation acceptance flow for new users calls auth.checkSession() in the constructor when getToken() is truthy (to handle users returning from the consents gate), calls auth.getInvitation on init, shows a set-password form when isNewUser is true, then calls auth.activate which uses bearer-mode delivery (PATCH /auth/activate?delivery=body) to return the access_token directly. If getInvitation returns 404 and the user has a token, the component redirects to '/' to handle already-accepted invitation links.

For existing users accepting an invitation, if already logged in the component calls auth.acceptInvite directly; if not logged in it shows a login form, calls auth.login first, then auth.acceptInvite.
Team switching calls auth.switchTeam which hits POST /auth/switch-team?delivery=body returning a new token, updating the session immediately without a page reload.

The team detail page enforces a 5-minute invitation resend cooldown that counts down from the invitation's last send: each non-expired pending invitation's createdAt seeds the cooldown when the list loads (withLastSends), and a successful resend restarts it from that moment. A refused resend surfaces the service's reason (too many resends for this invitation, or too soon) via resendError. The cooldown is reactive in zoneless Angular — a now signal ticks every 30 seconds so the Wait {n}m label and the disabled Resend button stay accurate, because Date.now() is not a reactive source.

In team management, member removal and role changes update the local member list only after the server confirms the change; owners cannot remove themselves because their own row renders no role dropdown or remove button.
Team deletion reloads the team list after success; if remaining teams exist but none is active, it auto-switches to the first remaining team before navigating to /teams.
The Account component loads the profile via auth.checkSession on init, then patches the form with firstName from profile.name and lastName from profile.surname; email is read-only.
currentPassword is intentionally not required at the form level for password change because OAuth users may never have set one; the backend only verifies it when the account actually has a password.
The isOAuthUser computed signal checks the socialAuths array on the raw user response to determine whether to show the hint about leaving current password blank.
The consents gate is triggered when a server-side Guards rule responds with HTTP 451 to any request including /users/me during session restoration.

consentsOnError is registered with provideRhAuth as the onError callback in app.config.ts, so it sees every API failure including session restoration — this is how the app distinguishes 'blocked by consents' from 'signed out'.
The ConsentsGate component sits in app.html outside the router-outlet, which is essential because authGuard cancels navigation when session restore fails, so nothing inside the outlet would render.

The consents gate overlay shows two checkboxes (Terms of Service and Privacy Policy) that both must be checked to enable the accept button; the request carries no versions — the server's permission mergeRequest stamps both document versions and the timestamp.

On successful consents acceptance, the gate performs pathname-aware navigation: if on an auth page (/auth), window.location.assign('/') navigates to home; otherwise window.location.reload() reloads the current page, preserving in-progress flows like invitation acceptance rather than losing them.
The sign-out action in the consents gate clears the consentsBlocked signal before calling auth.logout, so the next user to sign in on the same tab does not immediately see the overlay.
The consentsBlocked signal is a plain module-level signal (not a service) because consentsOnError is passed to provideRhAuth while the injector is still being built.

The Shell header contains no team switcher: team switching lives entirely on the /teams page, and the header avatar menu only displays the active team name derived from auth.teams().find(t => t.active).
The /teams/new route provides team creation: NewTeam submits a team name to auth.createTeam(teamName) and navigates back to /teams on success.
The forgot-password flow routes both success and error responses to the same confirmation state, so the UI never reveals whether an email is registered or whether the request failed.

When a verification link is expired or invalid, both the Verify page error state and the Login page's token_expired message direct the user to Forgot password, whose flow also verifies the account — the current recovery path for a dead verification link.

The setup script derives the service's accounts feature toggles from the same environment.dev.ts the app imports (registration and verification from emailRegistration, password-reset from passwordReset, invitations from teamInvitations, oauth from oauthLogin), so app and server flags are stated once and cannot drift.

The setup writes APP_NAME (env APP_NAME, default 'Ulabase Starter') into the branding feature config — the name on the sign-in page and in every email the service sends — reading the current config first so console-set color and logo survive the full-config replacement.

The setup sets the accounts frontend-url and frontend-app-url to APP_URL, which is where verification, reset and invitation email links point and where a verified or signed-in user lands after the backend redirects with the token fragment.

The Google OAuth credentials step is included only when the app offers Google (oauthLogin on and oauthProviders including 'google'); client-id and client-secret are resolved from GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET only when not already stored on the service, so a re-run against a configured service needs no secrets in the environment.

The setup adds the app origin to the origin-allowlist's allowed-origins (installing the feature if missing), appending rather than replacing so a service reached from more than one origin keeps them all.

appPointsAtService runs last in the setup: it writes the service URL into the apiUrl line of environment.dev.ts only after every other step is in place, so a setup that stops halfway leaves the connect-your-service screen rather than a sign-up page that fails.
